coverage_requirements.summary: The shared bounded-I/O crate owns product-neutral file and transport safety without business dependencies.
The shared identity crate owns product-neutral validated identifiers and their stable scalar wire representation.
The narrow Gewyvern install-contract crate owns strict installation and retirement wire semantics across product planes.
The project status subsystem owns schema validation, exhaustive architecture coverage, and machine-readable progress views.
The stable Gewyvern runtime owns evidence reconstruction and machine-facing validation contracts.
The Linux-first runtime owns eBPF attachment, collection, and physical-host proof.

The gewylang-compiler crate owns canonical lowering plus semantic-host and binding-materializer boundaries; gewylang-ir owns stable IR values and projection orchestration; Gewyvern owns only the concrete product adapters.
The gewylang-syntax crate owns bounded source loading, package expansion, parsing, syntax trees, and frontend summaries without product dependencies.
The GewyLang package shelf owns reusable protocol definitions and their validation surface.
The Leserpent 1.x bridge owns compatibility orchestration and persistence while Rust authority is adopted incrementally.
The Leserpent 1.x web console remains a supported compatibility frontend until shared command and query semantics replace browser-owned behavior.
Etragon owns optional advisory learning without replacing Gewyvern diagnosis or Leserpent orchestration authority.
The leselang-host-contract crate owns the product-independent ABI used by the language frontend and explicit product adapters.
The leselang-syntax crate owns lossless parsing and source diagnostics.
The leselang-hir crate owns validated names, types, effects, and capabilities.
The standalone language target separates core evaluation from product operations and proves embedding in an unrelated host; the OS shell remains deferred.
Post-2.0 typed computation and sequential automation must preserve budgets, ordering, recovery, authority, and GUI re-entry without claiming full shell parity.
The leselang-vm crate owns deterministic evaluation, continuation, and re-entry.
The leselang-command crate owns lowering into normalized command plans.
The leselang-ui crate owns neutral UI IR plus typed semantic event and Leselang effect round trips.
The leselang-observe crate owns validated, sanitized VM/runtime projection composition without becoming an execution authority.
The leserpent-domain crate owns commands, queries, events, identity, revisions, and capabilities.
The leserpent-runtime crate owns transactions, scheduling, replay, policy, and projections.
The leserpent-protocol crate owns Leserpent wire schemas, compatibility, and protocol-specific transports while re-exporting stable shared contracts.
The leserpent-adapters crate owns capability-gated external integrations and authenticated Gewyvern transports.
The leserpent-cli crate owns native operator CLI parsing, rendering, and transport-specific error semantics.
The leserpentd crate owns isolated local and remote runtime hosting.
The deployment-bootstrap boundary owns bootstrap-only credentials, daemon and Gewyvern installation state, and explicit authority handoffs before runtime mutation.
Gate 1 requires normalized domain semantics and protocol compatibility.
Gate 2 integrates the independently owned Leselang frontend with Leserpent VM replay and command lowering.
Gate 3 requires native CLI parity with Leselang and GUI command semantics.
Gate 4 requires neutral UI IR, a replaceable Avalonia vertical slice, and MIT open-source free core access.
Gate 5 moves durable authority into the Rust runtime and isolated daemon.
Gate 6 proves desktop and remote protocol/UI parity plus the declared minimum mobile entry and lifecycle contract.
Gate 7 freezes version-one contracts and requires security, performance, migration, packaging, and rollback evidence.
The optional production account lifecycle is retained as a post-2.0 prerequisite for future hosted subscription services, not as a free-core release gate.
Every gate maintains fuzz, parity, recovery, accessibility, transport, AOT, and benchmark proof.

Extend group result binding with bounded effectful loops and explicit host-effect recovery/cleanup. Sequential and flat parallel groups now drive one atomic tail or multiple captured successors, including typed scalar exits before or between captures; continuation schema 11 owns conditional group flows while schema 10 retains strict chains and journal schema 10 and older wire forms stay unchanged. Prefix plus longest cold path fits in 64 slots, all successor identities are reserved without early dispatch, and each raw receipt plus next request or scalar exit commits transactionally under original authority/shared fuel/deadline/output budgets. Recovery verifies successful predecessors, exact projections and frame continuity, accepts scalar terminals only where the saved body can return without another suspension, replays the first commit without recalculation, and retains live chains as one unit. Parallel prefixes remain independently leaseable with an all-success barrier and single-snapshot progress; native sequential conditional flows use the correlated single-presentation channel, while native parallel starts fail preflight before journals. Raw cumulative items/bytes and growing between-capture frames cannot bypass limits through scalar projection; unused reservations remain rowless without identity reuse. Typed booleans, acknowledged expected/field/value strings and pure helpers preserve closed versioned fields, hygienic bounded expansion and cold-path capability checks. Projection v3 preserves closed v1/v2 frames without synthesizing missing fields, and recovery checks saved strings against committed raw receipts. Text keeps its original operation domain, shared copy fuel and the 64 KiB image/plan bound; conditional aliases and cold branches use exact widened availability masks. Native text-driven form chains retain correlated acknowledgements without exposing private frames. Canonical node/action/form-input kind token strings use closed projection v4 while v1/v2/v3 remain byte-exact without synthesized fields, including mixed aliases and cold group members. Saved tokens must belong to their operation domain and match committed raw receipts; cross-domain arguments fail before successor creation. Kind-driven native waits and decisions preserve the same authority, fuel, deadline, cancellation, size and atomic replay fences without exposing private frames. Distinct optional_string scalars now preserve absent/empty/text through explicit construction, typed helpers/pure loop state, has_value and lazy value_or defaults. Four placeholder/unavailability operations export optional_expected through v5 while v1-v4 stay exact without synthesized fields. Explicit null/string payloads reject missing data, saved optional values match committed raw receipts, and only original optional-text host domains accept them directly. Contained text retains original domain/4096-byte scalar limits and copy fuel, output/image/plan bounds, deadlines, cancellation and transactional successor/terminal replay; native nullable waits/defaults never expose private frames. Exact contains/starts_with/ends_with predicates and zero-based Unicode scalar char_at now compose with pure helpers/loops, optional defaults and saved atomic/group bodies; empty patterns match, large indices remain bounded and out-of-range access is absent. Eager operands and full-input scan/character materialization fuel preserve cold typing, original host validators, old binary wire, projection v1-v5, schemas 1-11 and journal schema 10. Native text-selected form prefixes retain correlated acknowledgements without private frames; SQL rollback and first-commit replay remain fenced. Bounded ordered string_list data now supports strings/split/append/join/item_at and pure type-preserving fold, including filtering and nested aggregation. Lists retain 64-entry and 4096-byte aggregate bounds, closed bounded decoding, explicit optional indexing, source-order constructor evaluation and hygienic accumulator/item scope. Fold prepares the collection and initial state once, preflights a literal 0-64 limit without truncation, and charges shared copy/scan/iteration/materialization fuel without expansion or mid-loop suspension. Durable list locals and terminals reuse existing continuation schemas, journal version and closed projection vocabularies; native confirmed-text filtering reaches forms through correlated acknowledgements without private frames. Group all-success barriers, original host-domain checks, deadlines/cancellation and transactional SQL rollback/first-commit replay remain fenced. Reusable effectful functions now compose whole-flow/tail calls and explicit result binds through bounded normal-return splicing into existing HIR; atomic, group and typed data returns retain existing flow-shape and projection contracts. Pure signature arguments evaluate once in declaration order; hygienic result/group/accumulator/item locals and cold type/capability checks prevent caller capture and hidden effects. Every cold return reserves caller nodes/depth/canonical text before cloning, with no dynamic call stack or source/function table on restart. Existing wire schemas, original authority/fuel/deadline, raw-output/frame limits, SQL rollback and first-commit replay remain fenced, including native conditional helper-to-form acknowledgements. Operands, helper arguments and pure loops/folds/recovery remain effect-free; group members require prepared atomic flow; arbitrary nested result bind values gain no implicit call ABI. Prepared atomic helpers and expanded pure bind/choose now compose seq/all/repeat members only when every cold path has exactly one uniform HostOperation/result signature. Entire groups resolve synchronously in flattened order before effect/group identity allocation; later argument, domain or fuel faults admit no member. Parameter signatures evaluate once in declaration order, local scopes stay isolated and repeat reserves all expanded preparation nodes including constructor entries before cloning. Bounded iterative signature inspection rejects oversized/uniformity violations without unchecked recursion. Journals retain resolved atomic requests only; named projections, all-success barriers, original authority/revision/fuel/deadline, cancellation and first-commit replay remain unchanged. Native sequential helper-group projections reach forms through correlated acknowledgements; prepared parallel debugger starts still fail preflight before journals. Multi-step/result-capturing and group-returning helper members remain rejected. Selected named groups now export identical mode, ordered names and HostOperation signatures through pure conditional selection and helper returns, never a union of members. Only selected preparation executes; cold type/domain/capability and full expansion checks remain required. Structurally bounded iterative inspection rejects missing, reordered or mixed-mode signatures. Journals save the selected resolved graph without guards/helper tables; restart never reselects or refills budgets. Named member projections retain existing pure/tail/captured/conditional bodies, all-success barriers, cancellation/deadline/output limits and transactional successor rollback/retry with first-commit replay. Native selected sequence-to-form proofs retain correlated receipts/revisions without exposing private frames; native parallel starts remain fenced before journals. Existing continuation schemas 1-11, journal 10 and projections v1-v5 remain unchanged. Prepared atomic result binding values now accept pure bind/choose preparation, including selected atomic helper calls, only when every cold path produces exactly one uniform HostOperation/result signature. Captures and group members share bounded iterative inspection; hidden captures, multiple effects and pure operand effects remain rejected. Preparation locals never escape into saved frames; selected requests are resolved before suspension, future selections run after validated predecessor receipts, and committed requests are never reselected on restart or replay. Each capture consumes one graph slot under existing atomic/group chain and conditional-exit bounds. Group recovery verifies the same prepared signature at its exact capture position; parallel all-success barriers and closed legacy field availability remain unchanged, including cold paths. Original authority/revision/shared fuel/deadline, output/frame limits and cancellation remain fenced. Predecessor receipt plus successor or terminal SQL writes roll back together; pure uncommitted selection may retry from immutable inputs, and concurrent workers commit exactly one successor. Native result-driven focus-to-form and early-exit receipts preserve correlated identities/revisions without private frames or new GUI endpoints. Continuation schemas 1-11, journal 10 and projection vocabularies v1-v5 remain unchanged. Selected data-returning functions now compose pure choices of direct helper calls and pure data fallbacks into typed caller joins. Different supported helper topologies return one bounded data type; selected-only signature arguments, hygienic locals, cold return reservations, parallel barriers and transactional first-commit recovery retain existing schemas. Native single/sequential helper-to-form paths use correlated receipts; selected parallel starts still fail preflight before journals. Arbitrary nested effectful binding values remain rejected. Generic nullable/container types remain deferred. Pure calculation recovery does not catch host, authority or resource failures or refund fuel. Pure scalar loops run under shared fuel without mid-loop suspension. Current prefix groups prepare every parameter before the first suspension, not from earlier step results. Group capture inside atomic chains, result-capturing/multi-step computation as group members, mixed all/seq, multi-presentation debugger batches and a full shell remain unimplemented.

Preserve frozen-scope query, command and presentation re-entry with strict identity binding, long-lived worker adoption, barriers, attempt fencing and budget continuity. Eligible dispatches use fewer delivery attempts plus numeric admission order, retaining fixed-cohort progress and explicit exhausted-only LSV4017. Trusted host limits gate pending dispatches and active leases transactionally across shared workers, reject whole initial batches without partial publication, expose typed Idle versus Backpressured claims and authoritative read-only pressure, and bound request restoration while preserving duplicate idempotency. Scheduler faults use LSV2500-2503 without aliasing legacy merge validation LSV2401-2404. Imports commit durable identity watermarks with records; consistent startup validation repairs retained effect/group identities after validating cold reservations against the original watermark, leaves metadata unchanged on invalid state, and preserves higher metadata through compaction. High imported IDs cannot launder unallocated cold reservations; deleted legacy identities cannot be reconstructed. Already admitted groups and tails drain under lower limits; retries release lease slots but retain pending capacity. Busy SQLite claims do not materialize queued payloads, and active capacity inspection stops at its ceiling. Native debugger VMs apply a 64-pending/one-active policy without enabling parallel GUI starts. Policy is reapplied by the host, not persisted in wire formats or guaranteed against differently configured trusted workers. RootAdmission now owns one immutable pre-admission request, retries only LSV2501 with bounded deterministic exponential backoff and total attempts, pins submission/execute deadline, avoids VM/journal entry before due time, and consumes/releases input on terminal outcome. Clock faults leave state unchanged; local cancellation cannot cancel admitted work; shared workers recheck transactional capacity. Handles are not cloneable/deserializable, persisted ingress or accepted-effect replay, and native debugger starts do not opt in automatically. Hosts still own aggregate ingress/CPU bounds, wakeups/jitter, fair resource lanes, execution/cancellation identity and persisted cross-journal command mapping. Outbox/admission APIs do not add hidden queues, timers, worker pools, callback preemption or a tenant security boundary; continuation schemas 1-11 and journal 10 remain unchanged.
Preserve complete current-domain lowering, explicitly reject frontend-local effects, and retain CLI/Leselang/plan parity as orchestration operations are added.
Preserve the complete 62-atom presentation UI IR, Rust-owned canonical source, and the prohibition on frontend-owned command lowering; add atoms only for a concrete frozen-scope gap.
Retain physical Linux x86_64 evidence for the three maximum-capacity WebSocket cycles and bounded slow-session isolation, including exact idle, active, reclaimed, and restart FD/task baselines.
Preserve the stable Gewyvern adapter and secret-store boundary; introduce future external systems as separate typed adapters.

Retain physical Linux x86_64 lifecycle evidence and the authenticated debugger VM vertical; active sessions remain deliberately process-bound while cancellation audit is restart durable inside the bounded 64-journal horizon.
Preserve the stable macOS and Linux orchestration contract; treat WinRM as optional post-2.0 work only when Windows becomes an active native target.
Preserve the stable provisioning and retirement identities while future target platforms add independent native transport proofs.
Preserve stable local/remote command parity and zeroized credential handling; platform-native transports remain optional additions behind the authenticated HTTPS contract.

Preserve the complete MIT open-source desktop control path without account dependence; after 2.0, validate the optional production account lifecycle before introducing the first future hosted subscription service.

Keep dual-mode loopback HTTP and reviewed-CA HTTPS registration under real-TLS, wrong-CA, restart, import/export, cleanup, and frontend package regression; retain physical Linux remote-target proof as release evidence rather than ambient trust authority.

After 2.0, review the six candidate built-in catalogs and both 12-key official-pack expansions with native speakers, then extend only typed static UI copy without translating opaque operator data and refresh packaged multi-host evidence.
Preserve the shared remote/mobile entry, secure-storage, lifecycle, adaptive-layout, native rendering, and AOT contracts through 2.0; add production signing and physical-device breadth after 2.0.

Preserve MIT licensing, zero price, source availability, and account-independent access for every current core capability; only newly introduced future hosted services may require both an account session and an exact entitlement.

blockers.summary: The v2 producer and strict Rust verifier are complete, but the final macOS NativeAOT bundle has not yet completed a real system-browser login, credential-vault refresh, reconnect, and local logout against the reviewed Team Silvortex production issuer.

cells.next_gate: After 2.0 and before introducing the first future hosted subscription service, configure the final macOS NativeAOT bundle with the reviewed production issuer, run --prove-silvortex-account after final signing, and accept the evidence only after gewyvern_leserpent_release account-proof verifies both the executable and exact Info.plist digest against that same bundle.

Preserve the frozen 2.0 contracts and ship-ready release-gate baseline; expand the independent physical-host and kernel matrix with community evidence, and keep Apple notarization, future hosted-account proof, and long-tail language review on their explicit post-2.0 tracks. Later 2.x maintenance releases must validate this baseline without renumbering the ten historical patch slots or relaxing the closure-work whitelist.
Keep every named deterministic proof shelf green through 2.0; expand host/device/platform coverage and retain production signing/notarization evidence after 2.0.

blockers.summary: No production deep-learning runtime, model artifact pipeline, training/evaluation loop, or reproducible inference evidence is integrated; current learning behavior is a dependency-light advisory baseline.
The sidecar remains optional and less mature than Gewyvern's built-in diagnosis.

cells.next_gate: Keep the advisory boundary additive while integrating a reproducible deep-learning runtime, versioned model artifacts, training/evaluation gates, and retained inference evidence.
Keep schema v3 stable, recalibrate priorities with dated evidence, and require architecture additions to declare authoritative coverage in the same change.
